newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up on spreading, firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up on spreading, firmer cash.

text.p: Further unwinding of bear spreads combined with support from firming cash markets to again boost CME lumber futures, traders said.

Shorts continued to roll out of November which added to demand prompted by the recent bottoming action in the cash market. Reports that cash spruce prices were firming, possibly to the $365 to $375 per tbf area, prompted further buying interest in futures late, traders said.
Cash spruce fell to $366 Friday, a $66 decline from the recent high set on September 13. Cash prices fell $16 last week before stabilizing.
Traders also cited a firmer technical picture. November went up to fill a gap in the chart at $361 left from the break in September.
Lumber closed $5.10 per tbf higher to $0.10 lower with only distant July off. November was up most at $363.50 and January up $1.40 at $371.00 per tbf.
